items.title_orig: Geezer Butler, Anthrax’s Scott Ian, Mike McCready among new names for Tom Morello’s stacked ‘Power To The People’ line-up
items.article_text:
Tom Morello in New York City on May 12th 2026. CREDIT: Danny Clinch

Black Sabbath‘s Geezer Butler, Anthrax‘s Scott Ian, and Pearl Jam‘s Mike McCready are among the new names confirmed for Tom Morello‘s ‘Power To The People’ event. See the line-up below.

The festival is due to take place on Saturday October 3 at Merriweather Post Pavilion in Columbia, Maryland, and is billed as “a day of peace, love, justice and music”.

Bruce Springsteen, Foo Fighters, Joan Baez, System Of A Down’s Serj Tankian, Dave Matthews, Brittany Howard, Dropkick Murphys, Jack Black, Cypress Hill, Killer Mike and more were announced in the initial wave of acts in May.

Now, Morello has shared another batch of artists scheduled to perform. These are the aforementioned Butler, Ian and McCready, as well as Nathaniel Rateliff, Stephen Stills, State Radio and The Last Internationale.

Check out the updated line-up poster here:

Morello himself will also be taking to the stage at ‘Power To The People’, which will “bring together artists, fans, activists, organisations and community leaders for an unforgettable day celebrating the power of music and collective action to inspire change”.

Attendees can engage with nonprofit organisations, advocacy groups, artists, and community partners in the festival’s Freedom Village, too. A portion of the proceeds from all ticket sales, plus 100 per cent of the net proceeds from VIP tickets, will be donated to good causes.

These causes are VoteRiders – a pro-democracy, pro-voter organisation working to restore and strengthen democracy by eliminating confusing and restrictive ID-related barriers to the ballot box – and HeadCount, which will also be on site to help fans register to vote and learn more about how to participate in upcoming elections.

“The ‘Power To The People’ festival is about freedom, justice, equality and rock and roll,” said Morello in a statement.

“It’s about the power everyday human beings have when they come together through music, art, community, and action. We’re honoured to bring this incredible lineup to the DC area for a day that celebrates the spirit of activism, creativity, and hope.”
